origin.description: Fill braces from a list or data frame by calling glue_data.

arguments.name: .x
arguments.text: A list or data frame. Its names are visible inside the braces.
Unnamed strings are the template. Named arguments override .x.

arguments.name: .sep
arguments.text: Text placed between the template strings before interpolation.

arguments.name: .envir
arguments.text: Where names that are not in .x are evaluated.

arguments.name: .na
arguments.text: Replacement for a missing piece. The default is the letters NA.

origin.details: This is glue_data with a small set of arguments. Columns are recycled to one length. The result has one string per row.
origin.value: A character vector with the same length as the longest input.
origin.example:
cat(as.character(str_glue_data(
  list(name = c("Mazda RX4", "Datsun 710"), hp = c(110, 93)),
  "{name} has {hp} hp"
)), sep = "\n")

translation.description: Fill braces from a dict by calling glue_data.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A dict of names. Each value is a column the braces can see.

arguments.name: parts
arguments.text: Unnamed strings are the template. Named arguments override x.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: Text placed between the template strings before interpolation.

arguments.name: envir
arguments.text: Extra names. Names in x override these, and named arguments override x.

arguments.name: na
arguments.text: Replacement for a missing piece. The default is the letters NA.

translation.details: str_glue_data calls glue.glue_data. A dict stands in for the data frame. Columns recycle to one length.
translation.value: A list of strings, one per row. A missing piece is stringi NA.
